Body.Content:
Multiple factors (including seasonal adjustments, promotions, and market dynamics) can influence a product's active sales price, causing it to fluctuate over time. Businesses need a reliable way to detect and act on these changes. For example:

Retail stores must update shelf labels promptly to reflect the latest prices.

E-commerce websites must alert shoppers about price drops for items in their shopping carts, driving conversion.

Unified pricing management now provides price change tracking that automatically identifies items whose prices have changed since the last tracking run. Instead of comparing the full catalog each time, the system captures only those items that changed price within a specified time window.

Key benefits

Automated price change tracking provides the following key benefits for organizations looking to improve their pricing processes:

Automated change detection: Eliminate the need for stakeholders to manually identify which items have undergone price changes.

Delta-based tracking: Only items whose prices have changed since the last tracking run are surfaced, reducing noise and focusing attention on what matters.

Improved performance: By scoping reports to changed items only, reports generate significantly faster than full-catalog reports.

Feature components

The price tracking feature includes the following components:

Price change tracking data entity: All detected price changes are recorded to the price change tracking data entity, making them available for external reporting and downstream integrations.

Delta price reports: Price managers can now generate price reports that include only items with price changes since the last report generation, streamlining the review process. The reports are generated directly from within Unified pricing management.

GA date: December CY2026

Preview date: October CY2026
